correctness.summary: In the point-hyperplane nonincidence graph, legality on the point side is exactly strict growth of the selected-point span and total domination of hyperplanes is exactly full span; dually, legality on the hyperplane side is strict decrease of the intersection and total domination of points is zero intersection. Thus every total dominating sequence contains exactly d vertices from each bipart and has length 2d. Degree, connectedness, false-twin-freeness, and the recursive deletion property follow from elementary finite-dimensional linear algebra.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Prior work covers total 4-uniform crown graphs, a projective-plane-linked total 6-uniform family, nonexistence for odd k, and a connected total 8-uniform example. The 2021 paper explicitly left connected examples for all larger even k as an open direction. Searches across total-uniform, Grundy-total-domination, projective nonincidence, design, and hypergraph-covering formulations did not locate the arbitrary-dimensional construction or completed existence spectrum. The graph family itself is classical and is not claimed as new.

value.summary: The theorem settles the connected existence spectrum exactly: connected total k-uniform graphs exist precisely for positive even k. It replaces separate small-k constructions by one projective nonincidence mechanism valid in every dimension and provides infinitely many regular false-twin-free examples for each fixed even k at least 4.

limitations: The result is an existence theorem, not a classification of all total k-uniform graphs.
No minimum-order or minimum-degree claim is made.
Projective nonincidence graphs are classical; novelty is restricted to their total-uniformity property and the resulting existence spectrum.
The finite verification treats prime fields only, although the proof covers every prime power.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge; differently indexed finite-geometry, design-theory, thesis, or hypergraph-covering literature remains a residual risk.
